blogs.title: Atypical Dyskeratosis Congenita: Beyond the Mucocutaneous Triad in Young Adults
blogs.description: Often focusing on the classic mucocutaneous triad (nail dystrophy, leukoplakia, reticulate skin pigmentation), physicians may miss Telomere Biology Disorders (TBD) when these features are absent. This post analyzes the clinical presentation of the PARN-positive patient, emphasizing the importance of screening for TBD in young adults presenting with unexplained pancytopenia, premature greying, and multi-organ fibrosis when classical signs are missing.

blogs.title: PARN Variants and Pulmonary Fibrosis: The Undervalued Respiratory Sign of Dyskeratosis Congenita
blogs.description: Telomere biology disorders are increasingly recognized to manifest as Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF) or telomere-related pulmonary fibrosis and bone marrow failure (PFBMFT4). This post discusses how pulmonary fibrosis in young adults is often misdiagnosed as primary IPF or inflammatory myeloid, and how identifying a PARN variant—or considering telomere testing in the absence of classic genetics—should be the standard for hematology.

blogs.title: B12 and Folate Deficiency: Complicating the Hematologic Diagnosis in Marrow Failure Syndromes
blogs.description: Ineffective erythropoiesis is common in Telomere Biology Disorders, presenting with markers like dimorphic anemia and basophilic stippling. This post explores the overlap between true nutritional deficiencies (B12/folate) and telomere dysfunction, explaining why B12 repletion alone often fails to resolve underlying marrow failure and necessitates genetic evaluation for persistent cytopenia.

blogs.title: Variant of Uncertain Significance in TBD: Where Clinical Phenotype Validates Genomics
blogs.description: Genetic testing often yields a Variant of Uncertain Significance (VOS), creating diagnostic uncertainty in TBDs. This post uses the PARN c.613T>C case to illustrate how clinical-side 'hypothesis testing'—specifically matching the VOS to a classic phenotype like telomere-related fibrosis and bone marrow failure—can effectively establish a diagnosis even with uncertain genotypes.

blogs.title: Genomic Risks and Survivorship: Management of Mendelian Premature Ageing in Patients
blogs.description: Once a TBD diagnosis is confirmed, management shifts from acute treatment to long-term surveillance and survivorship. This post covers the critical counseling steps for families, the risk of bone marrow transplantation, the surveillance required for hepatic and pulmonary fibrosis progression, and the reality of curative versus supportive care options in TBD.
